correctness.rationale: The observation is exactly the five multiplicities for one-zero, one-one, two-zero, mixed, and two-one compositions. For nonconstant words these determine the symbol counts and the two run counts by \(a=z-r_0\), \(b=o-r_1\), and \(t=r_0+r_1-1\). Alternation gives the exact feasibility condition \(|r_0-r_1|\le1\), and positive compositions of symbol counts prove converse realization and the class-size formulas. Summing all feasible run profiles gives the stated parity formulas for every \(n\). The bundled verifier independently reconstructs literal observations for \(131070\) words through length \(16\), checks \(1020\) classes and singleton identities, and checks the arithmetic formulas through \(n=500\).

value.rationale: The result gives a complete all-length solution of the first nontrivial constant observation length in a model introduced specifically to study partial composition readout. It determines both the exact optimal code size and every ambiguity-class multiplicity, rather than only a construction or a finite table. The parameter \(r=2\) is the natural base case of the published constant-\(r\) question, and the full class structure is reusable for coding, ambiguity analysis, and testing larger-\(r\) methods.
